summary: Demonstration/comparison file for the deep embedding of Cooper's TTR (paired with TTR_theorems_shallow.v). Part A re-proves, against the model-relative inductive witness judgment of TTR_types.v, results both embeddings can state: the 'every man runs / John is a man / John runs' inference (universal premise as a meta-level hypothesis), one concrete instance of record-type width subtyping, and the Cooper A6-A8 subtyping laws (meet below both conjuncts, join above the left disjunct, singleton subtyping, transitivity). Part B states what only the deep embedding can: types stored as record values and recovered (VType reification), computed merges of record types via rt_merge_simple (right-override on label clash), provable uninhabitedness of a type in a model, a self-acknowledged stub of relabelling equivalence (length equality only), decidable equality for basic types only, and cross-model possibility/necessity of inhabitation. 18 theorems, all Qed, zero axioms; most Part B theorems close by reflexivity on concrete data.

determination_rationale: Mechanical application of rubric section 4 to this file's evidence: only a partial formalization exists here — the set-theoretic substrate is rendered as ordered association lists (the rubric's canonical 'changed', acknowledged in the TTR_base header and not discharged by permutation lemmas), merge right-overrides instead of taking Cooper's meet on common labels, and relabelling is a self-acknowledged stub. The determination is per this pilot's evidence, not TTR's ceiling: the axiom-free deep embedding of the witness judgment shows the A2-A8 core transfers cleanly, and the file's real finding is architectural — TTR's types-as-first-class-values (Part B) is exactly what forces reification and defeats a shallow embedding. A fuller formalization proving relabelling, the proper merge, and permutation invariance could plausibly upgrade TTR to slight_modification.

artifact_classes.description: TTR stores types as values (VType inside records, val_to_type) and quantifies over models of type assignments; Coq admits this only via deep reification — the shallow/deep split this file exists to demonstrate is itself the class-(ii) evidence

labelled sets and records as association lists: no native unordered finite maps, no coercive record subtyping or relabelling; the ordering artifact is admitted in TTR_base's header and never discharged
decidable type equality exists only for basic types (ttrtype_eq_basic); full RecType equality is undecidable because RF_dep fields embed Coq functions Val -> TTRType
